name: Arrange
description: Four audio tracks of bounced clips on a timeline
changelog: 0.26.0: everything by itself (core 2.26). With the song stopped every seq track ARM is not on that is not frozen as it is freezes -- the one ARM left, one gone stale after a tempo turned or a kit loaded --, a failed freeze tried again later; an element block only the engine can bake (its kit tracks frozen at another tempo) is rebaked by itself after 3 s untouched, the note saying which and why, instead of waiting for EDIT > Rebake now; a Pitch sound that would not load is asked for again and said; the song list pages (24 a page, from the open song's, Back / More) so every song can be opened. Requires core 2.26.

0.25.0: elements -- the song around them (core 2.25). With the song stopped and no pad played for 5 s Arrange tells the engine it may bake the other songs' blocks of an element changed since; a block whose element changed under it (a new tempo, a kit saved) plays as it was and says old until EDIT > Rebake now, which enters and leaves its element with the processing box over the lanes. A bake under way shows on its block. Requires core 2.25.

0.24.0: elements -- arrangements inside the song (core 2.23). EDIT > New element here lays a four-bar element on a free audio track and opens it; Element from library lays one already made. An element block is ice blue with a layers glyph and its title (dimmed, not baked, until its first leave); CLIP EDIT on it opens it as the song, the context row becomes the breadcrumb SONG > ELEMENT 1 (three levels at most, ... for the rest, a tap goes up to that level), and the power button's click goes one level up, freezing and baking what changed, with the processing box saying how far. Requires core 2.23.

0.23.0: MIX looks like a DAW's mixer -- each strip has the track's number and kind (or name) in its colour, PAN (C / L25 / R40, a tap on its reading centres it; kept with the song, core 2.21 SongTrack::pan), the fader with the track's stereo meter beside it (after the fader and pan, the lanes' scale: green, amber from -6 dB, red from -1), the dB, and M and S side by side; requires core 2.21

0.22.0: an audio track's input sheet (a long press on its header) has MONITOR: the input it records heard live on the speakers and jacks, or not -- the Mixer's MONITOR at all or off for that input's channels (MIC+LINE both), shown in the Mixer and kept with its desk; absent for the pads, heard anyway; requires core 2.20 (IInputMonitor)
0.21.1: an audio take round a loop says how many passes it kept -- the last is on the track, the others are clips to pick with EDIT (core 2.19). Requires core 2.19.

0.21.0: + ADD TRACK > AUDIO opens nothing: the empty audio track is armed and REC records its input over the song from the playhead (core 2.18 ArrangeAudioTake) -- after the count-in, from the next bar line while the song plays, on its own in an empty song -- and lays the take on the track when REC, STOP or PLAY ends it. A long press on an audio track header picks its input -- MIC, LINE, MIC+LINE, USB, PADS -- and arms it, MIX in the same sheet; an unnamed audio track shows its input (AUD MIC). ARM and Input in an audio track menu. No DUB onto audio. Requires core 2.18.

0.20.2: a new kit or Pitch track opens nothing: it stays picked and armed on an empty lane (core 2.16.1: no empty block over the whole song), REC records the pads into it and CLIP EDIT opens its seq view. A Pitch track with no instrument picked yet still opens Pitch Play, where one is. Requires core 2.16.1.

0.20.1: BOUNCE renders as a freeze does (core 2.14) -- off the clock, a looping block's two passes, nothing rendered for a track already frozen -- and shows in the processing box (BOUNCING TRACK n), the header saying BOUNCING... Requires core 2.14.

0.20.0: a freeze shows in the processing box over the lanes, as a time stretch does -- FREEZING TRACK 2, render 1 of 3, 40 % -- and core 2.13 renders it off the clock where the board can. Requires core 2.13.

0.19.1: fits under the 40 px top bar (crosspad-gui 2.4): the key row sat 5 px under it -- the screen is laid out from the export's 30 px bar -- and the screen is 200 px tall, not 210. The key row is 2 px under the bar, the lanes 28 px, the tool row 2 px higher.

0.19.0: auto-freeze starts the moment ARM moves on -- a new track added -- with the song stopped, not 3 s later; the header shows the whole freeze, FREEZING 2/5 40%. Core 2.12 renders only the blocks that changed or are new: a block the same as another, or as at the last freeze, is found on the card. Requires core 2.12.

0.18.2: a track being frozen says how far on its header -- FREEZING 45% -- from the freeze's render (core 2.11 renders a looping block's two passes, so it is seconds, not the track's length). Requires core 2.11.

0.18.1: auto-freeze waits for 3 s with the song stopped and ARM left alone, so a track added and recorded at once is not frozen first; REC and DUB cancel a freeze as PLAY does (core 2.10.1). Requires core 2.10.1.

0.18.0: + auto-freeze -- the seq track ARM leaves is frozen once the song stops (core 2.9 freezeTrack): its engine alone into a file the song plays in its place, so only the armed track costs an engine. Its header says FRZ in ice blue, FREEZING... while it is made; arming it, or changing its notes, sound or the tempo, plays it live again. PLAY cancels a freeze, made again at the next stop. Requires core 2.9.

0.17.3: a Pitch track's notes play whenever its instrument is up, whoever holds the screen -- the seq view of a Pitch block showed the notes and played nothing, with Arrange gone and the song stopped.

0.17.2: the pads play an armed Slice (second kit) track again after the kit picker or the seq view -- a screen that popped past the pads' logic left Arrange believing it was still pushed. Requires core 2.8.

0.17.1: a new kit or Pitch track takes the scene just added (AudioSong::sceneForNewSeq), not the sequencer's active one -- while the transport ran that was still the Drums track's, and adding a Slice track moved the Drums notes onto it. Requires core 2.8.

0.17.0: + ADD TRACK offers AUDIO or KITS; KITS is PERF, DRUMS, SLICE or PITCH, two by two, each kit picked from the browser's list of its kind. A Pitch track plays beside two kit tracks (core 2.6: its own route), so a song holds Drums, Slice, Pitch and audio at once; the pads play the Pitch instrument only while its track is armed. Requires core 2.6.

0.16.0: two kit tracks, each playing a kit of its own -- ADD TRACK > SEQ > Kit opens the kit loader (the first kit track's kit is the song's, the one the pads and the Sampler play; the second's is its own, in a second engine beside it), and a kit track's menu opens it again to change it. While two kits are up each plays five voices, the ten the card streams cleanly. ARM, the dot on a seq track's header after S and M, which sit on the number's line now -- all three only show, a touch on the header opens its menu, where they are keys: REC and DUB take onto the armed track, and here the pads play its kit. A kit track without a name shows its kit's. A block with notes of its own MOVEs between the two kit tracks. A track's menu is keys, two a row, as large as a dialog's BOUNCE and CANCEL, so it fits the screen and is easy to touch. FOLLOW is a right arrow, not the word, and the keys after it have most of their width back. Requires core 2.2.

0.15.1: builds on core 1.70+/gui 1.28+ and on core/gui 2.x (>=1.70.0,<3.0.0 and >=1.28.0,<3.0.0) for the merge window; a root deleted before the app's teardown is handled (gui 2.0 calls destroy with none)

0.15.0: FOLLOW on the context row, beside the position: on (lime, as it opens) the lanes scroll with the playhead while the song plays; off they stay where they were put, so a block can be edited while it plays, and turned back on they go to the playhead at once. Kept across openings of the screen. The keys after it are a little narrower to make the room, and the position while playing reads bar 2/4.

0.14.0: CLIP EDIT on an audio block opens that block in the Recorder -- the one picked, else the one under the playhead -- to trim it and put it back where it was. A power-button click no longer spends a level on letting go of the picked block: back is window, region, MOVE, keys, so every click is one step out; the hidden level left clicks that seemed to do nothing.

0.13.0: REC and DUB on the top bar record the pads onto the seq track from the playhead (core 1.58 ISongEngine::recordSeq): a REC becomes a block of its own notes from the playhead's bar, as many whole bars as it ran (a STOP a beat past a bar line ends it there), the seq blocks under it gone; a DUB adds to the blocks it plays over and makes blocks where there were none; with LOOP over a region the take goes round it, the first pass replacing it and every lap after dubbed in and heard on the next. The playhead stands where the take stopped, so the next REC is the next part. While pressed the playing song punches in and out. A song with no seq track gets one, playing the kit, on the first free track. Seq blocks are drawn from their own notes and labelled SEQ (a block that still plays the track's scene says which); DUP copies a block as a clip of its own from its first edit; the lanes are drawn on ahead of a take running past the last block, and the playhead is red while one records. CLIP EDIT on a seq block opens the seq view on that block; requires core 1.58.

0.12.0: EDIT is two keys -- the timeline's EDIT beside SYNC (the menu: a clip from the library, cut, the loop region, copy / paste / duplicate, merge, the song's length) and CLIP EDIT at the foot, which opens the selected track where it is made at a click (the sequencer, Pitch Play or the Recorder), no hold any more. A track's header is the export's track head, variant A (80 px): "01" in the type's colour over the name (RENAME in its menu, kept with the song; AUD / KIT / PITCH until it has one), S over M at a touch (and in the menu, for the encoder; solo silences the others, seq track included); a stereo meter of ten segments a side beside each lane, which ends before it; requires core 1.57 (SongTrack name/solo, ISongEngine::trackLevels). While stretched or repitched blocks wait to be fitted to a new tempo, a box over the lanes says PROCESSING TIME STRETCH with the blocks left and the current one's percent -- or that they wait for STOP while the song plays. UNDO / REDO at the top of the timeline's EDIT, with the steps there are: every change of the arrangement -- a block moved, cut, deleted, a merge, a bounce, a new tempo, M / S, a name -- one step a burst (core 1.57 ISongEngine::undo).

0.11.0: an audio track's menu (a tap on its header) has TIME STRETCH: OFF, STRETCH or REPITCH -- its blocks keep their bars through a change of the song tempo and play their audio fitted to them, the pitch kept (stretch) or moving with the tempo as on a turntable (repitch); the song engine renders a copy of each into the song's clips/.stretch/ while nothing plays, the block plays as recorded until its copy is ready, the status line counts what is left, and the block's waveform fills its bars, as the copy that plays does; requires core 1.57
0.10.0: a Pitch track opens in Pitch Play -- the same screen as the MODE map's Pitch -- instead of the seq grid; a kit track still opens the seq view. The 'plays with' sheet says so.

0.9.0: the status line sits in the status bar, centred where the CrossPad logo was (gui 1.17 statusbar_show_title), and the row it took goes to the tools at the foot: as tall as the screen leaves them, in the larger font, spread across the width; MOVE reads its axis as two arrows; requires gui 1.17

0.8.0: every block shows its clip's waveform under its name, at the speed it plays -- a file shorter than its block ends early, one made at another tempo shows where its beats fall; read from the card while nothing plays, once, and kept in the song's .peaks/ (core 1.34 clipPeaks); requires core 1.34

0.7.0: the song window exports the song to Ableton Live 12: <name>.als in the song's folder, which becomes a Live project -- four tracks, every block a clip on its bars at the song's tempo, faders, mutes and loop carried over; a report says what was left out; the songs list and the song window are lists under a header whose left end is the way back -- the open song marked, a click on it edits it, + NEW at the top, the song's settings a row each; requires core 1.33

0.6.0: MIX -- the four tracks' levels, a strip each side by side as on a desk: a tall fader in dB (-inf, 0.6 dB a step, unity at 90 %, +6 dB) and M, heard at once and kept with the song (core 1.31 saves a burst of commits once); requires core 1.31
0.5.1: MOVE and the song tempo: a value being turned reads dark on the accent: the text colour sits on the button, which is the only thing ever EDITED, not on its label

0.5.0: the song window deletes the open song -- asked once more, Keep it first -- and the first song left opens instead, or a new one; the tempo row no longer outlives its window (a rename finishing wrote to it after it was freed); requires core 1.30 and gui 1.15
0.4.1: builds on the PC against LVGL 9.4 (0.2.1 merged in); requires core 1.25 and gui 1.15

0.4.0: MOVE across tracks with arrows at the block; EDIT menu: a loop region (L/R turned, LOOP goes round it), copy / paste / duplicate x2 of the region, merge tracks or all tracks into one clip, song length; requires core 1.25 and gui 1.15

0.3.0: a click on a block takes the encoder to MOVE/DUP/DEL (MOVE is turned a bar per detent, the next click comes back; DUP and DEL come back at once; the power button's click too); wider track numbers; the songs list edits the open song's tempo and name, as requests; requires core 1.23 and gui 1.13

0.2.0: project list, clip list and opening a song are requests to the song engine (core 1.21 ISongEngine), filled in when the card answers; a song that cannot be read is left untouched; blocks drawn per track; the selection follows the exact block an edit moved
0.1.0: Generated from the CrossPad app template
